citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility has a part-time attending veterinarian but does not have a written program of veterinary care (PVC) . A written
program of veterinary care ensures that the animals receive adequate veterinary care. The facility must ensure that the
formal arrangements for employing an attending veterinarian include a written program of veterinary care.
***Correct by July 8, 2026.

At the time of the inspection, the licensee did not have a written contingency plan in place. A written
emergency/contingency plan is required to ensure animal health and well-being in the event of an emergency or disaster.
Without a proper plan animals could suffer illness, injury or death due to unpreparedness during an emergency or
disaster. The licensee must develop, document and follow an appropriate plan to provide for the humane handling,
treatment, transportation, housing and care of their animals in the event of an emergency or disaster.
***Correct by July 8, 2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the environmental enhancement/enrichment plan for non-human primates (lemurs) has not been
created by the facility and approved by the attending veterinarian (AV). The lack of an AV-approved environmental
enrichment plan for the lemurs does not ensure their environmental and social needs are being adequately provided. The
plan must be developed to address the social and environmental needs of the lemurs and approved by the attending
veterinarian.
***Correct by July 8, 2026.

Inspectors observed two areas in enclosures that were not maintained in good repair and could cause injury to animals:
-An enclosure containing the Sika deer and goats had a bent T-post (with sharp edges) and panel points protruding where
deer or goats could contact them.
-In the NW corner of the alpaca area (where the alpacas/sheep/zebu/Sika can cross a culvert) there was partially buried
chain-link fence on top of the culvert with wire points sticking out of the soil that animals could contact or step on.
Panel points, T-post points, and buried wire with sharp points could cause injury. The facility must maintain housing
facilities in good repair to protect animals from injury.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the written environmental enhancement/enrichment plan for birds had not been approved by the
attending veterinarian (AV). The documented plan addressed some of the species at the facility, however did not address
all species at the facility. Lack of an AV-approved environmental enrichment plan covering all bird species does not
ensure that environmental and social needs are properly being provided. The plan must be developed to address the
social, environmental and special considerations for all birds at the facility and approved by the AV.
***Correct by July 8, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Scott Welch, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
